text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A fight between opposition and ruling party legislators mars the presentation of 1997/98 (July/June) state Budget by Finance Minister Musalia Mudavadi.
- Following taxation measures announced by the finance minister Kenyans will pay more for fuel and kerosene but will pay less in direct taxes.
- The Supreme Council of Kenya Muslims presents a memorandum on land grabbing, immigration and constitutional reforms to President Daniel arap Moi.

- Opposition parliamentarians say they made their point as far as the call for minimum constitutional reforms is concerned by disrupting Finance Minister Mudavadi's budget speech and say they will continue to push for reforms.
- Three gangsters steal about 500,000 shillings ($9,090) from a commercial bank in the capital Nairobi.
- A bomb scare temporarily disrupts proceedings at the Nairobi law courts.
- Two opposition parliamentarians censor their colleagues for engaging in what they called a bar-like brawl during the state Budget presentation.
- The Electoral Commission expects to register eight million voters by the end of the voter registration exercise on Sunday.
- Moi says that the freedom of worship guaranteed by the constitution should not be misused to suit individual whims.

- With the general elections drawing near, an alarmed President Moi is seeking solace and backing from members of his ethnic Kalenjin group in the hope that if they show a united front, he will be able to use them as a bulwark against the growing rebellion in the ruling party.
